title: Typing Blog: Speed, Accuracy and Keyboard Guides
description: Practical guides on typing speed, accuracy, average WPM by age and touch typing technique, written for anyone who wants faster and calmer hands.
lead: Practical guides on speed, accuracy, technique and what the numbers actually mean. Exam-specific claims cite the official notice, and every guide shows when it was last updated.

p: Every article is written for people who type for a living or are preparing for an exam, and each one ends with something you can practise the same day. We cover the mechanics of speed, the maths behind WPM, realistic benchmarks by age and profession, and the technique fixes that remove plateaus.

If you are brand new to touch typing, start with the beginner guide and work through the lessons alongside it. If you already type quickly and want to break a ceiling, the accuracy and speed articles will be more useful.

title: About Typinger: The Typing Test and Game Arcade
description: Learn who builds Typinger, why the site mixes serious typing tests with arcade games, and how WPM, accuracy and leaderboards are calculated here.
lead: Typinger is a free typing site built on one idea: practice only works if you come back tomorrow.

p: Typing is the one computer skill almost everybody uses every day and almost nobody trains. Many people learn by accident and settle into a routine without ever practising the skill deliberately. The tools that could fix that are usually either clinical drill software that nobody opens twice, or games with no real measurement behind them.

Typinger is the middle path. Underneath it is a strict measurement engine: standard five character words, keystroke level accuracy, honest timing that starts on your first key. On top of it sits an arcade — ten games, three difficulty levels, a daily challenge and achievement badges — so that the practice is something you actually want to do.

Speed is always WPM = (correct characters / 5) / (seconds / 60), and accuracy is always ((keystrokes - errors) / keystrokes) x 100. We never count incorrect characters toward speed and we never hide errors you corrected, because the point of a measurement is to be useful rather than flattering.
Game scores multiply WPM by accuracy so that careful typing wins, and every result is stored against the game, the difficulty and the date, which is what makes the dashboard chart meaningful.

blocks.h2: What is free and what an account adds
ul: Free for everyone: all typing tests, all practice drills, the twelve touch typing lessons and all ten games.
With a free account: saved game WPM history, per game statistics, achievement badges, daily challenge results and leaderboard placement.
No ads interrupt a test, and we never require payment to see your score.

p: Typinger is built and operated by Aditya Karn, the Founder & Operator, based in Noida, Uttar Pradesh, India. He is responsible for the code, the practice passages and the editorial pages. You can reach him at support@typinger.in or through the contact form.

Typinger is not affiliated with the Staff Selection Commission, the Railway Recruitment Boards, the MP CPCT programme or any government recruitment body. A practice score is feedback for training, not an official result or certification.

blocks.h2: How we research and update guides
p: We use primary documents where a claim depends on a rule: official notifications, rulebooks, government releases and the exam body's own notice board. When a figure belongs to a specific cycle, the article names that cycle and links the source.

Practical guides are different. They are written from established touch-typing instruction, the site's own measurement rules and the published research or workplace guidance listed on each page. We do not present them as the results of a controlled experiment, a user survey or a personal training study. Targets such as 95-97% accuracy, ten to fifteen minutes a day and 40-50 WPM are editorial practice benchmarks, not universal standards.

Every article shows a published date and, where it has been revised, an updated date. If a rule changes, we correct the article rather than leaving an old figure presented as current. If you spot an error, email support@typinger.in with the page and the correction.
Our practice passages are original text written for Typinger. They are not copies of official exam passages, and a practice score does not reproduce an exam's scoring software.

Advertising, when enabled, does not determine which tools or articles we publish. We do not accept payment for a favourable review, a claimed pass mark or a testimonial. Where a page discusses an external product or exam, we say what we can verify and link the primary source.

Advertising is currently disabled. Before any ad is served, we will configure a Google-certified consent management platform where required, keep ads out of active tests and lessons, and update the privacy policy to describe the real data flow. Enabling an ad unit is not the same as configuring consent.
Corrections are published on the page itself. We do not silently change a figure that affects an exam decision; we update the date and, where the change is material, explain what changed.
We do not invent qualifications, study results, testimonials or user numbers. The author bio lists only the role and location we can verify.

faqs.q: Is Typinger really free?
faqs.a: Yes. Every test, lesson and game is free and unlimited, and an account is optional. We do not charge for results or lock features behind a subscription.

faqs.q: Do you sell my typing data?
faqs.a: No. We store the minimum needed to show your history and leaderboards, and we never sell personal data. The privacy policy explains exactly what is kept.

faqs.q: Can I suggest a new game or feature?
faqs.a: Please do. Use the contact page; feature requests from users are the main source of our roadmap, including difficulty levels and the daily challenge.

faqs.q: Which keyboards and layouts are supported?
faqs.a: Any physical keyboard and any layout, including QWERTY, Dvorak, Colemak and Devanagari input methods for the Hindi test.

faqs.q: Do you have a mobile app?
faqs.a: Not yet. The site works in any modern browser, and we recommend a physical keyboard for a fair measurement of speed.

faqs.q: Who owns Typinger?
faqs.a: Typinger is built and operated by Aditya Karn, Founder & Operator. He is responsible for the service and can be contacted at support@typinger.in.

title: Contact Typinger: Support, Feedback and Bug Reports
description: Send the Typinger team a message about bugs, leaderboard issues, feature ideas, account problems or partnership enquiries using the contact form.
lead: Questions, corrections, bugs, leaderboard disputes or a feature idea — email us or use the form below. Typinger is built and operated by Aditya Karn in Noida, Uttar Pradesh, India.

p: Use the form on this page or email support@typinger.in. Include a valid email address if you want a reply. For account and data requests, write from the email address on the account so we can verify the request.
ul: Bug reports: tell us the page, your browser and keyboard layout, and what you expected to happen.
Account help: include the email address on the account so we can verify the request safely. Never send us your password.
Leaderboard reports: include the game, the difficulty and the player name; verified cheating is removed by our moderators.
Feature ideas: describe the practice problem you are trying to solve rather than the solution, and we will look for the simplest fix.
Corrections: include the page URL and the sentence you believe is wrong. A primary source helps us verify the change.
Press and partnerships: mention the audience and the format you have in mind.

p: A lot of questions are already answered on the about page, in the blog guides, or in the FAQ at the bottom of each test page. If your score did not save, check that you were signed in before the run finished, because results are attached to an account at the moment they are submitted.
If a game feels unresponsive, make sure the game area has focus by clicking it once, and check that your browser is not blocking the Web Audio sounds used for key feedback.

faqs.q: How do I send a message?
faqs.a: Use the contact form on this page or email support@typinger.in. Include a valid email address if you want a reply.

faqs.q: My score did not save. What happened?
faqs.a: Scores are attached to your account when the run finishes, so a run started while signed out will not save. Sign in first, then play, and the result will appear in your dashboard history.

faqs.q: How do I report a suspected cheater?
faqs.a: Use the contact form and choose Leaderboard report. Include the game name, difficulty and the player name shown on the leaderboard. Our moderators can flag or remove individual results after review.

faqs.q: Can I delete my account and data?
faqs.a: Yes. Use the contact form and choose Account or data request. Include the email address on the account so we can verify the request, and we will delete the account, its results and its badges permanently.

faqs.q: Do you accept guest posts?
faqs.a: Occasionally, if the author genuinely knows the subject and the article is original. Send a short outline rather than a finished draft.

faqs.q: Do you publish a support email address?
faqs.a: Yes. The support address is support@typinger.in. The contact form remains available if you prefer not to use email.

title: Privacy Policy: How Typinger Handles Your Data
description: Read what Typinger stores, which cookies are active now, how analytics and advertising consent will work, and how to delete your account.
lead: Last updated November 2026. We store what is needed to show your typing history, nothing is sold, and the current build runs no analytics or advertising scripts.

ul: Account data: your display name, email address, a securely hashed password and the date you registered. Passwords are hashed with bcrypt and are never stored or transmitted in readable form.
Result data: for each completed run, the game, difficulty, score, WPM, accuracy, duration and timestamp, plus whether it was a daily challenge.
Technical data: standard server logs, which include an IP address for abuse prevention and rate limiting on sign-in.

Analytics data: none at present. The current production build does not load Google Analytics or any third-party analytics. If a Google Analytics 4 measurement ID is configured in a future build, analytics will load only after you accept the analytics control, and the data will be limited to anonymised page and event measurements.

Advertising data: none at present. Google AdSense is not active and the site serves no ads. If advertising is enabled after approval and the required consent platform is configured, Google AdSense may collect cookie and device data to serve and measure ads, as explained below.

p: Typinger sets an httpOnly authentication cookie and a refresh cookie when you sign in. These are strictly necessary for the site to keep you logged in and cannot be disabled while you are signed in.

Your browser's local storage holds non-identifying preferences: your theme choice, the sound mute toggle, your preferred difficulty and your analytics choice. The current build does not set analytics or advertising cookies. If analytics is enabled, cookies are set only after you choose Accept; you can withdraw by reopening Privacy choices in the footer, which stops further analytics collection. Advertising cookies, if ads are enabled, are controlled by Google's certified consent message where required.

Account and result data exists to run the features you asked for: your dashboard, your WPM chart, your achievement badges, the daily challenge board and the public leaderboards. Your display name is visible on leaderboards; your email address never is.

We do not sell personal data and we do not profile you for marketing. The current build does not send analytics or advertising data to third parties. If analytics is enabled, aggregate, anonymised statistics may be used to understand which tests are useful and to write articles, for example average speeds across difficulty levels.

Advertising is currently disabled. Typinger has no active AdSense units, and the AdSense runtime is not loaded. If advertising is enabled after approval, Google AdSense may use cookies to serve ads; Google's use of advertising cookies would enable it and its partners to serve ads based on your visit to Typinger and/or other sites on the Internet.

Before serving ads in the EEA, UK or Switzerland, we will configure Google's certified consent management platform through AdSense Privacy & messaging (or a Google-certified external CMP) and verify the consent signal. The site's own analytics control is separate and does not replace that CMP. You can opt out of personalised advertising at adssettings.google.com or aboutads.info. Ads will not be placed inside an active typing test, lesson, game, exam or Daily Challenge; they will appear only after a result or inside editorial content.

You can request a copy of your data or ask us to delete your account at any time through the contact form using the email address on the account. Deletion removes your profile, results and badges permanently, and leaderboard entries disappear with them.
Children under 13 should use Typinger with a parent or guardian and should not create an account with a personal email address.
You can also email support@typinger.in with the subject line "Data request". We may ask you to verify control of the account before deleting it.

blocks.h2: Security and changes to this policy
p: Traffic is served over HTTPS, passwords are hashed with bcrypt, sign-in is rate limited after repeated failures and administrative pages require an admin role. No system is perfect, so please report any security concern to us directly.
If this policy changes we will update the date at the top of this page. Material changes will also be announced on the blog.
This policy describes the build at the date above. If analytics or advertising is enabled, we will update this policy before those scripts go live.

faqs.q: Do you use tracking cookies?
faqs.a: The current build does not set analytics or advertising cookies. It uses essential authentication cookies when you sign in. If analytics is enabled, it will load only after you accept the analytics control, and you can withdraw in Privacy choices. If ads are enabled, Google's certified consent message will control advertising cookies where required.

faqs.q: Can I use Typinger without an account?
faqs.a: Yes. All tests, lessons and games work signed out, and nothing is stored about you beyond standard server logs.

faqs.q: Where is my data stored?
faqs.a: In a managed MongoDB database used only by Typinger. Access is restricted to the application and to site administrators.

faqs.q: How do I delete my data?
faqs.a: Use the contact form and choose Account or data request, or email support@typinger.in from the address on the account. We will permanently delete the account, its results and its achievement records after verification.

faqs.q: Is my password readable by anyone?
faqs.a: No. Passwords are hashed with bcrypt before storage, so neither we nor an attacker with database access can read them.

title: Terms of Service: Rules for Using Typinger
description: The terms for using Typinger, covering accounts, fair play on leaderboards, acceptable use, intellectual property, liability and how disputes are handled.
lead: Last updated November 2026. Use the site, practise hard, do not cheat the leaderboard.

p: By using Typinger you agree to these terms. If you do not agree, please do not use the site. We may update the terms as the product changes, and the date above reflects the current version.

You are responsible for keeping your password safe and for everything done through your account. Give us an email address you control, choose a display name that is not offensive or impersonating someone else, and do not share logins. We may suspend accounts that break these rules or that are used to attack the service.
Sign-in attempts are rate limited to protect accounts, so repeated wrong passwords will temporarily lock sign-in for that email.

Leaderboards only mean something if the scores are real. Submitting results produced by scripts, macros, text expanders, modified clients or network tools is prohibited, and our moderators may flag or delete any result that is clearly not human typing. Repeated manipulation leads to account removal.
The daily challenge is validated on the server against the day's game and difficulty, so results submitted for the wrong combination are rejected automatically.

ul: Do not attempt to break, overload, scrape at scale, or gain unauthorised access to the service.
Do not use Typinger to store or transmit unlawful content, including in display names.
Do not resell access to the site or present it as your own product.
Automated access is allowed only for well-behaved search engine crawlers following robots.txt.

p: The Typinger name, interface, games, lesson material and articles are our intellectual property and may not be copied wholesale. You are welcome to quote an article with a link back, and to share your own result cards anywhere you like.
Typing passages include public domain and originally written text. If you believe something here infringes your rights, contact us and we will review it promptly.

Typinger is an independent practice website. We are not affiliated with SSC, RRB, MP CPCT or any government recruitment body, and we do not claim to reproduce their official software, scoring or qualification decisions.

Typinger is provided as is, without warranty. We aim for high availability but we cannot guarantee uninterrupted service, preserved scores in the event of a failure, or that measurements match any particular exam's official scoring. To the extent permitted by law, our liability is limited to the amount you paid us, which for a free service is zero.
These terms are governed by the laws of India, and disputes will be subject to the jurisdiction of the competent courts in India.

faqs.q: Can I use Typinger results in a job application?
faqs.a: Yes, and we recommend quoting a three or five minute result. Typinger is not an accredited certification body, so some employers will still run their own assessment.

faqs.q: What counts as cheating?
faqs.a: Any result not produced by you typing on a keyboard in real time: scripts, macros, text expanders, autocomplete tools or modified clients. Moderators can flag or remove such results.

faqs.q: Can my account be deleted without warning?
faqs.a: Only for serious abuse, such as attacking the service or repeated leaderboard manipulation. In other cases we contact you first using the email on the account.

faqs.q: May I embed Typinger tests on my site?
faqs.a: Not without written permission, but you are very welcome to link to any page, and links to specific tests are encouraged.

faqs.q: Do these terms change?
faqs.a: Occasionally, as features change. The updated date at the top of this page always reflects the current version, and significant changes are announced on the blog.

faqs.q: Is Typinger an official exam website?
faqs.a: No. Typinger is independent practice software. It is not affiliated with SSC, RRB, MP CPCT or any government body, and a practice score is not an official result.
